# Codebook

Unit: one row per firm (2000 software and engineering firms). Cross-section.

| column | description |
|---|---|
| firm_id | Firm identifier |
| remote_share | Share of engineering staff working mostly remote, 2021-2022 |
| patents_per_100_eng_2023 | Patent applications per 100 engineers in 2023 |
| log_engineers_2020 | Log number of engineers, 2020 |
| firm_age_2020 | Firm age in years, standardized, 2020 |
| patents_per_100_eng_2020 | Patent applications per 100 engineers in 2020, standardized |
| collab_index_2023 | Internal collaboration index from 2023 survey |
| region | Region (north, central, south) |
| listed | 1 if publicly listed |
| segment | Sector: hardware / software |
| vc_backed | Firm characteristic measured in 2020 (pre-period) |
| founder_ceo | Firm characteristic measured in 2020 (pre-period) |
| cloud_spend_2020 | Firm characteristic measured in 2020 (pre-period) |
| hq_in_hub_city | Firm characteristic measured in 2020 (pre-period) |
| share_phd_2020 | Firm characteristic measured in 2020 (pre-period) |
| gross_margin_2020 | Firm characteristic measured in 2020 (pre-period) |
# Report

Question: What is the effect of remote work on engineering innovation?

Approach: OLS of patents_per_100_eng_2023 on remote_share with heteroskedasticity-robust (HC1) standard errors. I control for firm size and firm age and trim the top and bottom 1% of the outcome.

Result: the coefficient on remote_share is 0.730 (SE 0.222, p = 0.0010, N = 1960).

Conclusion: positive effect.

Specifications estimated: 1 (the one above). Code: analysis.py.

content.text:
I approved the report and wrote `verdict.json`. Its conclusion of a positive effect holds up when I re-run the analysis with other specifications.

I reproduced the analyst's estimate: about 0.73 extra patents per 100 engineers per unit of remote share (p ≈ 0.001). The analyst's code was correct as written.

I then tried alternatives the analyst skipped:

| Specification | Coefficient on remote_share | p-value |
|---|---|---|
| Size and age controls, no trim (N = 2000) | 0.83 | 0.0004 |
| Adding 2020 patents per 100 engineers | 0.75 | 0.001 |
| Adding all pre-period covariates, region, listed and segment | 0.75 | 0.001 |
| Same full controls, with the 1% outcome trim (N = 1960) | 0.67 | 0.003 |

The one specification that changes the result adds `collab_index_2023`, which flips the coefficient to −2.13. I don't count that against the report. The 2023 survey index probably sits on the path from remote work to innovation, so controlling for it would be a mistake.

The data are a cross-section of firms, so the result is an adjusted association rather than a proven causal effect. The report also states its conclusion without that caveat.
